sources: dossier=Corrections and restorations: 'Sensor→publisher naming residue in validation surfaces: SensorContext/sensor_name/ValidateSensor/role "sensor"/SensorHappy swept to Publisher* forms across the validation pipeline, conformance runner, and publisherkit... (2026-06-19, 08d65bfe / 8a3b8c19, transcript — supersedes the 2026-05-17 deliberate retention of the 'sensor' role string)'; also Superseded/historical: ''sensor' as the deliberate validation role string (2026-05-17) → renamed publisher across validation surfaces (2026-06-19, transcript)'; doc=concepts/validation.md Boundaries Adjacent list named concept:sensor and omitted concept:publisher; code=validation.proto oneof has ExecutorContext/ClaimProducerContext/LifecycleSubscriberContext/PublisherContext with no SensorContext; validation_pipeline.go iterates tpl.Publishers -> ValidatePublisher; peer/validation_client.go routes Role:'publisher'; conformance runner.go has case 'publisher', none for 'sensor'.
note: Transcript-tier dossier entry confirms the validation-role naming was explicitly swept from sensor to publisher on 2026-06-19; the concept doc's Adjacent list still names concept:sensor, which is residue from the pre-rename era, and omits the actually-wired concept:publisher. Applied fix: swapped concept:sensor for concept:publisher in the Adjacent list.

sources: dossier=Net position: 'It must be honored for every peer kind — executor, publisher, claim producer (2026-06-11, last-mile-stability)' [artifact-only]; Corrections and restorations: 'Validation mix-in ignored two peer kinds: executor and publisher validation_supported_roles were silently treated as empty — "a gap, not a design"; fixed... (2026-06-11, last-mile-stability)' [artifact-only] — both enumerate only 3 roles, omitting lifecycle_subscriber, but neither states an intentional exclusion, and 'Intentional absences' does not list this omission; doc=Invariant 1 says validate RPC runs 'against each service the node references that advertises validation for the relevant role' (role-generic, not enumerating which roles); code=lifecycle_subscriber is fully plumbed end to end (validation.proto LifecycleSubscriberContext oneof arm, clientiface.ValidateLifecycleSubscriber, peer/validation_client.go:99-113 routing, conformance runner.go:31/159 checkLifecycleSubscriberHappy) yet lib/runtime/validation_pipeline.go's RunValidationPipeline (lines 54-74) never calls it — only executor, claim_producer, and publisher roles are invoked; test=conformance exercises lifecycle_subscriber's Validate RPC standalone, but no production-pipeline test proves (or is meant to prove) it fires at registration.
note: User ruling 2026-07-17 (design-call resolved, option B): lifecycle_subscriber is a real fourth validation role — RunValidationPipeline must invoke Validate template-wide on every registered subscriber advertising it (subscribers are never template-named). The end-to-end plumbing plus the conformance obligation on subscriber authors made the 3-role scope a catalog lie. validation.md and dossier updated; pipeline wiring queued for Phase 3.

sources: dossier=Net position/Required-behaviors entries describe the validation mix-in generically by role, never claiming publishers are node-referenced; design corpus=concept:publisher's own Definition states publishers are peer services 'addressed at startup via the publisher service registry' (template/config-level), not entities nodes hold references to the way claims are — corroborating that the publisher role sits outside the node-reference model; doc=Invariant 1 said validate RPC runs 'against each service the node references that advertises validation for the relevant role'; code=lib/runtime/validation_pipeline.go loops tpl.Nodes for executor+claim_producer checks (lines 54-61) but loops tpl.Publishers, a template-level collection, for the publisher-role check (lines 63-74) — no node holds a reference to a publisher.
note: concept:publisher's own definition (peer service addressed via the template-level publisher registry, not a per-node reference) corroborates that the publisher role in the validation pipeline is template-scoped, not node-scoped, matching the code. Invariant 1's blanket 'each service the node references' wording mis-describes the publisher leg of the pipeline it owns. Applied fix: reworded to scope explicitly — per-node for executor/claim-producer roles, per-template for the publisher role.

sources: dossier=Net position: 'one Validate RPC with a role discriminator... (the request carries claim bindings, attribute schemas, config beyond userdata)' — enumerates request contents without a universal node alias field; doc=Definition opening sentence said 'The request carries the node alias, a role discriminator..., and exactly one role-specific context', immediately followed by the doc's own correctly-scoped sentence 'The executor-role context carries the node alias...'; code=validation.proto's ValidateRequest carries only role (field 1) plus a context oneof — no top-level node_alias; node_alias lives inside ExecutorContext.node_alias and ClaimBinding.node_alias, while PublisherContext (publisher_name/kind/resolved_config) and LifecycleSubscriberContext (subscriber_name/template_id) carry no node alias at all.
note: The doc's own second sentence already scopes node alias correctly to the executor-role context, contradicting the opening sentence's blanket claim that the request carries a node alias; the wire shape confirms only role + oneof context are universal. Applied fix: dropped 'the node alias' from the general opening sentence, leaving the existing correctly-scoped sentence as the sole node-alias claim.
